items.note: Controlled experiment on a writing ideation task comparing LLM use from the start versus after independent ideation; LLM-first reduced the number of original ideas and lowered creative self-efficacy; abstract does not state random assignment or whether a no-AI arm exists.

System paper (Scideator) with a user study of computer science researchers comparing it with a baseline using the same LLM; reported outcome is 'creativity support', likely a self-report index, so it may be self_report_only at full text; N not stated.
Abstract calls itself a narrative literature review of AI-augmented design creativity; no systematic search or meta-analysis.

2x2 study (GPT-4o-mini conversational cues versus none, virtual versus in-person) with 172 participants in dyads brainstorming; cued groups' ideas were more topically diverse; abstract from Semantic Scholar, unit of assignment may be the dyad.

Meta-analysis of RCTs of AI interventions on cognitive, social-emotional, and academic outcomes; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar, Springer page); scope is broad AI, not specifically generative AI and creativity, so it may be out at full text.

Quasi-experiment with 36 students in immediate-AI, delayed-AI, and no-AI conditions on a collaborative problem-solving task; immediate AI produced more homogeneous solutions; below the 50-participant threshold and not randomized.

Exploratory study with 61 undergraduates comparing sketching groups with AI concept-generation groups; AI groups produced more and more varied ideas with homogenization; creativity of final concepts inconclusive; assignment method not stated.

Within-student pre-post design: 45 first-year architecture students refined a handmade design with AI visualisation tools, expert CAT ratings before and after; no randomized order or control group, authors call it observational; below 50.

Observational course data from 133 art students linking self-reported AI use to graded final creative performance with baseline and propensity-score adjustment; AI use not assigned, so it fits the codebook's non-random with/without-AI comparison; outcome is performance and authorship, not diversity.
Systematic review and meta-analysis on generative AI and student creativity; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC, Taylor and Francis page), classified from title.
